rationale:
Largest remaining error (B3c report §5.4, largest_remaining_error): confident noisy bona false alarms on the reference B3a-top5. They are 180 of 782 half_B noisy bona, 77 % of them at p_spoof >= 0.99. The largest localised block is by codec: heldout g726 36/129, heldout gsm 38/127, matched opus:qq 21/60 and opus:wechat 17/50, which together hold 112 of the 180. SNR 0 holds 40, the next block.

What the wave has ruled out so far:
- B3b (sampler, -0.83 [-1.46, -0.25]): exposure and the operating point.
- B3c (lambda 1.0, -0.77 [-1.31, -0.22], verdict.json): more invariance on the existing augmentation distribution. Heldout carried most of the loss, and the saturated tail sharpened.
The analyst concludes that the open levers are the coverage of the training degradation distribution and regularisation. `codec_random` is the next queued lever in wave.json, and the analyst ranked it first.

Why codec coverage is a real gap (derivation, computed from the two profile tables):
- The fixed profiles concentrate on high bitrates: 0.473 of draws are above 24 kbps, only 0.084 are at or below 12 kbps, and the mean is 24.43 kbps.
- The random profile puts 0.600 of draws at or below 12 kbps (mean 13.20). It raises the share of 40/60 ms frames from 0.143 to 0.667 and adds VBR modes and packet-loss hints.
- The two weakest matched codecs on B3a (full sets) are the low-bitrate apps: opus:qq (R_bona 68.69) and opus:wechat (72.12). The reserved heldout codecs g726 and gsm sit at 71.14 and 72.76. Low-rate, narrowband channel artefacts are exactly what the fixed table under-samples.

Constraints:
- One flag, in `allowed`, outside every coupled group. The consistency group (js, 0.3, both, --batch_size 8) is untouched, nothing forbidden or fixed is touched, and the run stays at 8 of max 10 epochs.
- Reserved ops are safe: the random profile still encodes only with libopus (assert_training_ops checks this at start-up). `-packet_loss` is a libopus encoder hint, not the reserved packet_loss filter. g726/gsm stay unseen, so any heldout gain must come from generalisation.
- The path was smoke-tested (b3wave README, "train j"). Codec failures print "failed (", which the early check forbids.

Why not the alternatives:
- snr_0_20 targets a smaller block (40 of 180) and is the natural iteration 5 if this one is null.
- SpecAugment targets over-fitting, a secondary symptom.
- lambda 0 is a recipe control with a smaller expected gain.
- A seed repeat is not warranted while configuration levers that the evidence supports remain.
hypothesis:
Heldout-codec and low-bitrate bona false alarms are a coverage problem. The model has learned "heavy low-rate codec artefact implies spoof" because the bona it saw in training passed almost only through mid/high-bitrate Opus: 0.473 of draws above 24 kbps and 0.084 at or below 12 kbps.

Randomising bitrate, frame size, VBR and the packet-loss hint per clip exposes bona and spoof alike to strong low-rate artefacts. Then:
- CE can no longer use the artefact level as a spoof cue.
- The paired JS at 0.3, with each view drawing its own random codec, makes the decision invariant across codec parameters. That is invariance on a wider distribution, not more weight on the same one, which B3c showed to be harmful.

Expected effect: the confident bona false alarms on qq/wechat drop because those conditions are now covered directly. g726/gsm improve through generalisation from the low-rate Opus artefacts, which share the band limitation and coarse quantisation. Spoof recall holds, because the synthetic-speech cue does not live in the codec artefacts.
falsifier:
Wave rule against B3a-top5 = 93.06 on half_B:
- Promote / positive: delta merge > +0.5, the paired-bootstrap CI excluding 0, and a clean F1 drop <= 0.5.
- Null: delta within +-0.5.
- Negative: delta below -0.5.

Mechanism-level refutations:
1. Codec coverage is not the limit: delta within +-0.5 AND full-set g726 / gsm R_bona within +-3 of 71.14 / 72.76 AND qq / wechat R_bona within +-3 of 68.69 / 72.12. Move to the SNR range (snr_0_20) or SpecAugment.
2. Covers seen codecs but does not generalise: qq / wechat R_bona up >= 3 while g726 / gsm move less than 3. The heldout codec errors are not explained by Opus parameter coverage.
3. Blurs a spoof cue: R_spoof down > 0.5 on matched or heldout. Random low-rate profiles mask the synthesis artefacts.
4. Lost the high-bitrate mass: matched opus:zoom / opus:lark R_bona down > 3, or a clean F1 drop > 0.5. Removing every > 24 kbps draw hurt high-quality channels. A fixed/random mix would need code, so it is out of this wave.
header_text:
B3d = B3a with one flag added: --aug_codec_profiles random. Every training clip still goes through one of the same 7 Opus app profiles (same app draw, cutoff and application). Bitrate is now drawn from {6,8,12,16,24} kbps, frame size from {20,40,60} ms, VBR from off/on/constrained, plus a packet-loss hint (0, or 5-20 %).

Everything else is identical to B3a:
- --consistency js --consistency_lambda 0.3 --consistency_pairs both, --batch_size 8 = 8 pairs = 16 clips/step;
- 8 epochs, LR 2.5e-6 warmup-cosine to 5e-7;
- sampler shuffle, CE weights 0.1 0.9;
- RTC aug + MUSAN, SNR 5-20 dB, loudness norm -23.
It runs ~8 h.

Evidence:
- B3a (JS 0.3) is the reference: merge half_B 93.06.
- B3b (sampler) was negative at -0.83 [-1.46, -0.25]: not exposure, not the operating point.
- B3c (lambda 1.0) was negative at -0.77 [-1.31, -0.22]: more invariance on the same augmentation distribution hurt heldout.
- On B3a-top5, 112 of the 180 half_B noisy bona false alarms sit in heldout g726 / gsm and matched opus:qq / wechat.
- The fixed profiles draw 0.473 of codec passes above 24 kbps and only 0.084 at or below 12 kbps. Random draws 0.600 at or below 12 kbps.

Target: low-bitrate and unseen-codec bona false alarms. g726 / gsm stay reserved, so any heldout gain must come from generalisation.

Rule against B3a-top5 = 93.06 on half_B: promote if the delta is > +0.5, the CI excludes 0 and the clean drop is <= 0.5; null within +-0.5; negative below -0.5.
